final_candidates.decision_summary: Corresponds to N501Y, the canonical affinity-enhancing RBD adaptation that adds aromatic contact with ACE2 Tyr41; strongest biological prior for enhanced cell attachment. WT residue N171 verified in the supplied sequence.
Corresponds to Q498R, which forms a favorable salt-bridge/electrostatic contact with ACE2 in Omicron-lineage RBDs and supports maintained-to-enhanced binding. WT residue Q168 verified.
Corresponds to E484K, an interface charge reversal observed across lineages that maintains ACE2 engagement; slightly lower confidence due to context-dependent effects. WT residue E154 verified.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are anchored in well-established ACE2-interface variant biology and remaining tools offer only indirect priors unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: This substitution corresponds to the repeatedly observed N501Y interface adaptation and introduces aromatic interactions that can strengthen ACE2 recognition. WT residue N171 was verified in the supplied sequence.
Corresponds to the well-validated N501Y ACE2-affinity-enhancing substitution; no contradicting evidence exists, so it remains top-ranked.
Corresponds to N501Y, the canonical ACE2-affinity-enhancing Spike adaptation at the receptor interface; aromatic gain at this position is well supported by variant literature as a biological prior.
This corresponds to E484K, an interface charge reversal associated in several lineages with altered and potentially enhanced ACE2 engagement. WT residue E154 was verified.
Analogous to E484K at the receptor interface; retains strong rationale for maintaining/enhancing ACE2 engagement.
Corresponds to E484K, an interface charge-reversal seen in multiple lineages with maintained or altered ACE2 engagement; retained as a strong interface-relevant candidate.
This corresponds to Q498R, which creates a favorable electrostatic interaction with ACE2 in known Spike variants. WT residue Q168 was verified.
Corresponds to Q498R, which forms favorable electrostatics with ACE2 in Omicron; remains a strong interface candidate.
Corresponds to Q498R, which forms favorable electrostatic contacts with ACE2 in Omicron-lineage RBDs; retained as a complement to N501Y-type enhancement.
A conservative aromatic-to-aromatic substitution at an interface-adjacent tyrosine may preserve receptor engagement while modestly changing side-chain packing. WT residue Y175 was verified.
Conservative aromatic substitution unlikely to disrupt binding; kept as backup below the top-3.
Conservative aromatic substitution near the interface; kept as a lower-confidence fallback but remains below the top-3 cutoff.
